slides.title: Professionals run a drill
slides.text: When an incident lands, professionals do not improvise. They run a drill with four moves: contain, preserve, report, recover. Your hand-sized version of it starts now.
slides.alt: Lock 5 at Pro: someone has a classmate's mailbox key, and a second message pressures you. Six drill tiles wait.

focus.cue: The drill in order: six tiles

slides.title: Contain the damage
slides.text: Contain means stop the bleeding first. Leave the fake page, and change the key from a clean device you trust, not from the screen that may have tricked you.
slides.alt: The drill begins: Stop and disconnect is placed first. Five tiles still wait to be put in order.

slides.title: Preserve the evidence
slides.text: Preserve means keep the proof: screenshots, the message, the time it arrived. Do not delete in embarrassment. Evidence is what lets adults and platforms act, and speed beats embarrassment, twice over.
slides.alt: Three drill moves in order: stop and disconnect, save the evidence, tell a trusted adult, fast.

focus.cue: Preserve: save the evidence, delete nothing

slides.title: Report, then recover
slides.text: Report to a trusted adult, your school and the platform. Then recover: a fresh passphrase on the hit account, and everywhere it was reused. That is the separate-keys lesson from Unit 2, paying off.
slides.alt: Five drill moves in order, up to change the key from a clean device. Only the one-line log is left.

slides.title: Run the whole drill
slides.text: You tapped a faked sender's link and typed your passphrase before the doubt arrived. Run the drill in order.
steps: Contain: leave the page, change the key from a clean device
Preserve: screenshot the page and note the time
Recover: new passphrase everywhere it was reused
slides.alt: The faked Post Office letter, reported: the name says Post Office, but the address and the button tell the truth.

focus.cue: A faked sender's button went somewhere else

slides.title: The one-line log
slides.text: Afterwards, Defenders write one line: what happened, what the drill caught, what changes. Incidents are tuition. The log is how the next Defender pays less for the same lesson.
slides.alt: Lock 5 open: the drill ran in order, start to finish. Calm work, and the skill it trained.

focus.cue: Lock open: calm work, start to finish
